items.author: Masudul Zarif
items.title: Bangladesh weighs tougher cyber law as AI-generated abuse targets women
items.summary: Bangladesh’s proposed cyber law targets AI-generated fakes, but critics warn broad provisions on rumours, defamation and disinformation could revive censorship and threaten online free expression, even as victims need protection.

items.title: Warning Signals: Venezuela and the Risk of AI-Powered Chinese Digital Authoritarianism
items.summary: A report by the Australian think tank ASPI warns that Venezuela could integrate Chinese artificial intelligence into its surveillance system and expand its digital control capabilities.

items.summary: The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. items.title: Volunteers from Poland remember how Poles opened their homes to Ukrainian refugees in 2022

items.author: Laura
items.title: Vote young yet govern much later: West African youth’s struggle for power
items.summary: Young people are deemed mature enough to elect their leaders, yet not to replace them. They drive political movements forward by voting, advocating, campaigning, and protesting, yet cannot run for office themselves.

items.author: Liam Anderson
items.title: Between two shores: The ‘Monhés,’ nationality, and a sense of belonging in Mozambique
items.summary: “Monhé” is not a nationality: a person of Indian origin can be completely Mozambican, foreign, or in some cases, stateless.
